content.comment_body: Hello, I'm looking for a way to detect if an analog input (4-20mA) is trending upwards or downwards. My setup involves filling a tank with a motorized valve—the more empty the tank, the more open the valve should be, and the reverse when the tank fills. I have two outputs to control opening or closing the valve. I'm planning to use an analog threshold function to assess tank levels, divided into ranges like 4-8mA, 8-12mA, etc. However, to decide whether to open or close the valve, I need to know if the tank level is going up or down. Any advice would be appreciated.

Hi, The code in the attached [document] shows how to check if an analog signal is rising or falling. This might not be a complete solution but could serve as a useful starting point. Take a look and let us know if it helps.
Here's my suggestion for your problem...

Storing the signal with update intervals is a clever approach! I initially tried a simpler method, but I find your solution more robust, especially when considering update rates. Observations: 1) Only one storage element is necessary—either B003 or B005 can be used. 2) Using SR blocks may cause issues when the value becomes steady. I suggest using a TOF block instead, with the TOF coil triggered by the original S and the TOR reset by the original R. Thanks for sharing your technique!

Thanks to [user_name] and 190B for the helpful suggestions. As [user_name] mentioned, these ideas make good foundations, and I'll likely use the latching relay approach since we need to switch on the valve until a set position is reached, at which point the output can be reset.
